speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned having chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination; to better understand your condition, how long have these symptoms been occurring, and do you experience any pain specifically during urination?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis (Bladder Pain Syndrome).

The patient's history of chronic pelvic pain relieved by voiding, combined with urgency, frequency, and dyspareunia (painful intercourse), strongly points to interstitial cystitis rather than a simple urinary tract infection. I will not perform further testing as the clinical presentation is classic for this condition.
